summary.text: A 58-year-old woman presented to a local hospital on May 12, 2024 with irregular vaginal bleeding for the past 8 months; pelvic ultrasound found a nodule at the right anterior urethra, and hysteroscopy with needle biopsy of the urethral mass showed malignant uterine growth and invasive carcinoma in the urethral mass. Her medical background was largely unremarkable. She was referred for further assessment and treatment.

At the treating facility she had ECOG performance status 1 on admission, moderate cachexia, bloodstained vaginal discharge, a vaginal wall mass, an enlarged uterus, elevated CA125 of 120 U/mL and normal routine laboratory tests. CT, MRI and echocardiography showed pulmonary nodules, a right atrial and ventricular mass and pelvic lesions. Pathology showed high-grade endometrioid carcinoma, MSI-H/MMRd; germline testing was declined. After review of her history, imaging and pathology, stage IVC MMRd endometrial cancer with cardiac and lung metastases was confirmed, and an MDT discussion was held.

Between May and October 2024 she received 6 cycles of paclitaxel, carboplatin and tislelizumab, with a grade 3 thrombocytopenia managed with thrombopoietin receptor agonists and dosage adjustment, although the paper also says no adverse events were reported. Imaging in November 2024 showed partial response, and 3 cycles of tislelizumab maintenance were given from November 2024 to January 2025.

Follow-up pelvic ultrasound in January 2025 confirmed continued resolution of pelvic lesions and CA125 fell from 120 to 25 U/mL. After maintenance treatment the cardiac metastasis was reported as eliminated, without surgery or radiation. As of February 2025 she was in good overall health with stable disease management and a progression-free survival of 9 months.

ambiguities.issue: The diagnosis sentence names the heart, lungs and vagina as additional cancer sites, whereas Table 1 and the CT response sentence name the urethra; other sentences describe a urethral mass, a vaginal wall mass and a nodule anterior to the vagina or right urethra.

evidence.quote: additional cancers affecting the heart, lungs, and vagina
May 2024 | Diagnosis | Stage IVC MMRd EC diagnosed with metastases to heart, lung, and urethra
a tender, poorly mobile mass (approximately 2 cm) in the anterior vaginal wall

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide whether the vaginal and urethral sites are one lesion or two, and do not infer that the vaginal wall mass, the urethral nodule and the nodule anterior to the vagina are the same or different lesions.

ambiguities.issue: Grade 3 thrombocytopenia during chemoimmunotherapy is stated, but the same paragraph says the patient reported no adverse events during the treatment.

ambiguities.issue: The cardiac metastasis is called confirmed in the diagnosis sentence, but the discussion states pathological confirmation of the cardiac lesion was not obtained and that a cardiac thrombus or benign cardiac mass cannot be entirely ruled out; it also describes extrinsic compression whereas the echocardiogram describes a mass attached to the walls with mild protrusion into the cavity.

evidence.quote: the diagnosis was confirmed as stage IVC MMRd EC with additional cancers affecting the heart, lungs, and vagina
Although pathological confirmation of the cardiac lesion was not obtained
The cardiac involvement represented extrinsic compression with patent outflow tracts

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer pathological proof of the cardiac lesion or exclusion of the differential diagnoses, and do not reconcile extrinsic compression with the intracavitary protrusion.

ambiguities.issue: Response is described with different degrees and sources: right cardiac mass vanished (imaging in November 2024), near-total resolution of the myocardial metastasis (cardiac CT November 12, 2024), partial regression versus marked regression of pulmonary disease, partial regression versus resolution of the urethral lesion, and complete radiographic resolution after maintenance (Table 2, discussion).

evidence.quote: Imaging conducted in November 2024 showed that the heterogeneous echoes in the uterus had resolved, the urethral hypoechoic lesion had decreased to 13 mm × 7 mm, and the right cardiac mass had vanished
(B) Cardiac CT shows near-total resolution of the myocardial metastasis (arrow).
A thoracoabdominal CT scan indicated partial regression of metastases in the lungs, urethra, and left iliac vessels, categorized as a PR (Fig. 2)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge these descriptions into one result, assume they refer to the same imaging study or modality, or equate partial regression, resolution and complete resolution.

article_limitations: Pathological confirmation of the cardiac lesion was not obtained (b00017); the cardiac metastasis is the authors clinical diagnosis and benign alternatives are not entirely ruled out.

The third metastatic site is named vagina in the diagnosis sentence and urethra in Table 1 and elsewhere; both are recorded as supported sites with an ambiguity (possibly one lesion), not as a source conflict.
Grade 3 thrombocytopenia is stated alongside a statement that no adverse events were reported; both are recorded as source_conflict and not resolved.
MSH6 is printed as negative in the case text and as partial loss in the discussion; both recorded as source_conflict.
The immunohistochemistry list prints "partial response (PR; 90%+)" and the PD-L1 score as GPS; printed wording is kept and not reinterpreted.
Response degrees differ across sources (vanished, near-total resolution, partial regression, resolution, complete radiographic resolution) and are kept as printed.
Values printed inside Figure 3 are pixel content in the visual submission only and are not recorded as separate facts.
Literature cases in the discussion and Table 2 (published reports) and general statements are not recorded as patient facts; the Table 2 present-case row is the index patient.
The statements that all management decisions were made with informed consent and that the patient perspective was not documented are administrative and not recorded as clinical facts.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the three JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.
No supplements are listed in the source.
